EPIC PLAN REVIEW #3 -> BLOCK, 1 blocking (a NEW, deeper one; pass-2's map-duplication blocker is resolved). Advisory count 6 -> 12.
BLOCKER (G6): jira_fields.py cannot relocate wholesale — it imports fit_text_to_adf_limit from the PINNED adf.py (used by _sanitize_description) and truncate_comment_body/_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS from the PINNED comment_limits.py (used by _sanitize_comment). Moving the file would make jira_family/ import adapters/jira/, inverting the very dependency direction the epic's own import contract (SS6) forbids. VERIFIED at jira_fields.py:18-26. The reviewer named only the adf.py half; the comment_limits.py coupling is a second instance of the same defect.
REMEDIATION #3: move by SYMBOL, not by file, and resolve the coupling with a contract the epic ALREADY introduces rather than a new mechanism — _sanitize_description's fit_text_to_adf_limit call IS the RichTextCodec seam (J3 aac8). So:
 - outright to jira_family/: _sanitize_label, _sanitize_summary, InvalidLabelError, _RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK, the value-map literals (none touch ADF/limits; _sanitize_summary is pure char truncation).
 - contract-parameterized into jira_family/: _sanitize_description (takes the RichTextCodec) and _sanitize_comment (takes the vendor comment-limit contract). Cloud builds those objects in adapters/jira/ from its pinned adf.py/comment_limits.py; DC builds wiki/plain-text equivalents in J6/J7. jira_family/ imports neither pinned module.
 - adapters/jira/jira_fields.py SURVIVES as the thin Cloud-side contract-construction site; ACLI callers re-point at the jira_family symbols directly, so no shim remains.
 - probe.py splits too: the pure classifier moves, but probe()/_resolve_env() stay in adapters/jira/ because they read Cloud's ACLI settings (Cloud-specific transport). identity.py still relocates whole.
 - Added a J2 AC: grep proves jira_family/ imports no adf/comment_limits/outbound_fields/acli* module. Added a fallback instruction: if J3's codec shape isn't settled yet, inject a minimal Callable[[str],str] — never import the pinned module from jira_family/ as a stopgap.
Note both adf.py and comment_limits.py are pure-stdlib (no imports beyond json/re/datetime/typing), so they are pinned by path-loading ALONE — nothing about their contents blocks the seam.
